summary: Changes the review requirements for adding DNSSEC algorithms and records to IANA registries. It extends RFC 6014 to cover hash algorithms for Delegation Signer records and NSEC3 parameters, and also updates RFC 5155 and RFC 8624. The aim is to make the process for these registries consistent.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9157 changes the process for adding certain DNSSEC algorithms and parameters to IANA registries. It makes the process consistent with other DNSSEC algorithm registries and warns readers not to treat registry inclusion as proof that an algorithm is safe.

subtitle: A change to how DNSSEC algorithms and parameters receive IANA registrations.

tldr.problem: Some DNSSEC registries still required Standards Action for DS and NSEC3 hash-related entries, while RFC 6014 had relaxed requirements for other DNSSEC algorithm identifiers.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9157 changes specified registration procedures to RFC Required and clarifies recommendations for algorithms defined in non-standards-track RFCs.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9157 is updated by RFC 9904. It aligns the listed registry procedures but warns that registry presence is not a security review.

today: RFC 9157 is updated by RFC 9904. It updates RFC 5155, RFC 6014, and RFC 8624.

sections.title: Aligning DNSSEC Registry Rules
sections.content: RFC 6014 changed the allocation procedure for DNSSEC cryptographic algorithm identifiers from Standards Action to RFC Required. However, registry procedures for DS hash algorithms and NSEC3 hash algorithms still said Standards Action. RFC 9157 changes the relevant requirements to bring them in line with the other DNSSEC algorithms.
sections.plainLanguage: Different DNSSEC registries had different approval rules. This memo aligns the listed DS and NSEC3 entries with the procedure used for other DNSSEC algorithms.

sections.title: Changes to Algorithm Guidance
sections.content:
RFC 9157 updates RFC 6014 so DS hash algorithms, NSEC3 hash algorithms, NSEC3 parameters, and NSEC3 flags fully described in an RFC can receive IANA identifiers.

It also replaces a paragraph in RFC 8624 to clarify that its recommendations cover algorithms defined in RFCs that are not on the standards track. An algorithm listed in the DNSKEY and DS registries but not mentioned in RFC 8624 may be implemented.
sections.plainLanguage: An RFC can describe eligible DS and NSEC3 entries for registry assignment. RFC 9157 also clarifies that the implementation guidance includes algorithms from non-standards-track RFCs.

sections.title: Registration Procedures
sections.content: In the NSEC3 Parameters registry, the procedures for DNSSEC NSEC3 Flags, DNSSEC NSEC3 Hash Algorithms, and DNSSEC NSEC3PARAM Flags change from Standards Action to RFC Required. In the DS Resource Record Type Digest Algorithms registry, the procedure for Digest Algorithms changes the same way. RFC 9157 is added as a reference in those registries.
sections.plainLanguage: Four registry procedures change from Standards Action to RFC Required. The entry must be described in an RFC for IANA to assign an identifier.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says the changed requirements make it easier to add both good and bad algorithms, and that the net security impact cannot be weighed. It warns administrators of signed zones and validating resolvers not to base security decisions on registry contents, because listed algorithms may not have had IETF review. Security choices should instead be informed by security literature.
sections.plainLanguage: Being listed in an IANA registry does not show that an algorithm is safe. The RFC advises readers to consult security literature when making security decisions.
